name: Sandworm
summary: GRU-linked actor repeatedly associated with disruptive and destructive operations against infrastructure, communications and regional adversaries.
description: Sandworm is one of the most consistently publicly attributed Russian military cyber actors. Joint advisories from the UK and U.S. governments connect Sandworm to GRU activity and link the actor to operations ranging from NotPetya to Cyclops Blink and other infrastructure-focused campaigns. Public reporting often shows a blend of espionage access, sabotage and strategic signaling.

sources.label: NCSC / CISA joint notice on Cyclops Blink
CISA Russia state-sponsored cyber threat publications

name: APT29
summary: Stealth-focused espionage actor commonly linked to the Russian Foreign Intelligence Service.
description: APT29 is best known publicly for long-term intelligence collection, cloud and email targeting, and highly selective post-compromise tradecraft. Joint advisories and government statements associate the group with the Russian SVR and with operations that emphasize persistence and information theft over noisy disruption.

sources.label: CISA / FBI / NSA advisory on Russian SVR cyber operations
NCSC advisory on APT29 targeting vaccine development

name: APT28
summary: Russian GRU actor known for aggressive espionage, credential operations and infrastructure abuse.
description: APT28 has been publicly tied by the UK and U.S. governments to Russia’s GRU Unit 26165. Public case material shows the actor using a mix of phishing, credential operations, router exploitation and bespoke tooling to support military and intelligence collection priorities.

sources.label: NCSC advisory on APT28 exploitation of Cisco routers
CISA advisory AA23-108

name: Storm-0558
summary: China-based espionage actor publicly tied by Microsoft to targeted email access using forged authentication tokens.
description: Storm-0558 entered public view after Microsoft disclosed an intrusion affecting customer email accounts in 2023. Microsoft described the actor as China-based, focused on espionage, data theft and credential access, with particular interest in government agencies in Western Europe and related individuals.

sources.label: Microsoft MSRC disclosure on Storm-0558
Microsoft Security analysis of Storm-0558 techniques

name: Volt Typhoon
summary: PRC state-sponsored actor known for stealthy access to critical infrastructure through living-off-the-land techniques.
description: Public reporting from Microsoft and later U.S. government advisories frame Volt Typhoon as a strategically important actor because of its focus on critical infrastructure pre-positioning. Rather than relying heavily on custom malware, the group is known for hands-on-keyboard operations and abuse of native tools to minimize detection.
objective: Espionage and potential pre-positioning for disruption

sources.label: Microsoft Volt Typhoon disclosure
CISA fact sheet for critical infrastructure leaders

name: UNC3886
summary: China-nexus espionage actor focused on edge, virtualization and high-trust infrastructure targets.
description: Mandiant has repeatedly described UNC3886 as a highly advanced China-nexus espionage group with strong tradecraft around virtualization and appliance compromises. The group stands out for targeting vCenter, ESXi and other difficult-to-monitor layers, then using custom backdoors and careful post-compromise steps to protect access.
aliases: No stable public government alias consensus
objective: Long-term access to high-value enterprise infrastructure

sources.label: Mandiant / VMware Product Security report on UNC3886 and vCenter
Mandiant report on UNC3886 espionage operations

name: Lazarus Group
summary: North Korean state-sponsored umbrella actor associated with espionage, sabotage, ransomware and financially motivated cyber operations.
description: Lazarus is one of the best known DPRK cyber group names in public reporting. The U.S. Treasury formally identified Lazarus, Bluenoroff and Andariel as agencies, instrumentalities or controlled entities of the Government of North Korea based on their relationship to the Reconnaissance General Bureau. Public casework spans WannaCry, destructive intrusions, financial theft and supply-chain activity.
objective: Revenue generation, espionage and strategic disruption

sources.label: U.S. Treasury sanctions targeting Lazarus Group
CISA guidance on the North Korean cyber threat

name: Turla
summary: FSB-linked espionage actor associated with the long-running Snake malware ecosystem and other stealthy collection operations.
description: Turla is publicly tied by U.S. authorities to a unit within Center 16 of Russia’s Federal Security Service. The group is widely known for long-lived espionage campaigns, covert routing infrastructure and carefully engineered malware families used against governments, diplomatic entities, journalists and research targets.

sources.label: DOJ announcement on Operation MEDUSA and Snake
NSA statement on Snake infrastructure identification

name: Salt Typhoon
summary: PRC-affiliated espionage actor associated in public U.S. government reporting with compromises of major telecommunications infrastructure and other network access operations.
description: Salt Typhoon is the industry name most commonly used for a PRC-linked espionage cluster associated with sustained access to telecommunications infrastructure. U.S. government reporting in late 2024 and 2025 described unauthorized access to commercial telecommunications providers by PRC-affiliated actors, and later advisory language noted partial overlap with activity commonly referred to as Salt Typhoon. The public picture emphasizes strategic intelligence collection, infrastructure access, and long-term operational persistence rather than noisy disruption.
aliases: GhostEmperor overlap discussed in some industry reporting
objective: Strategic espionage and long-term infrastructure access

sources.label: FBI and CISA joint statement on PRC activity targeting telecommunications
CISA advisory AA25-239A on China state-sponsored actors

name: UNC4841
summary: A well-resourced espionage actor identified by Mandiant in Barracuda ESG zero-day exploitation and assessed with high confidence to support the PRC.
description: UNC4841 came into public view through the exploitation of Barracuda Email Security Gateway appliances. Mandiant assessed with high confidence that the actor is engaged in espionage in support of the People's Republic of China. The campaign is notable for using network appliances as a covert access layer, then adapting malware and persistence quickly in response to remediation.
objective: Espionage via appliance compromise and durable persistence

sources.label: Mandiant on Barracuda ESG exploitation by UNC4841
Barracuda ESG vulnerability notice

name: APT27
summary: Long-running China-linked intrusion actor publicly associated in recent DOJ material with hacking-for-profit operations against U.S. and foreign organizations.
description: APT27 is a long-established China-linked intrusion set that has appeared in public reporting for years under multiple vendor names. In 2025, U.S. Department of Justice charging material tied alleged Chinese hackers with PRC government links to a years-long campaign targeting U.S. technology firms, municipalities, universities, defense contractors, think tanks, and other organizations for theft and later resale of data.
objective: Espionage, theft, and profit-driven intrusion under state protection

sources.label: DOJ press release on APT27-linked hackers-for-profit activity
DOJ broader charging announcement on PRC hacker-for-hire ecosystem

name: APT31
summary: China MSS-linked espionage actor publicly described by DOJ as part of a hacking program targeting dissidents, politicians, campaign staff, and strategic industries.
description: APT31 is one of the clearest examples of a China-linked group described in both private sector and government language as a long-running cyber espionage actor. U.S. Department of Justice material states that the APT31 Group was part of a cyberespionage program run by the MSS Hubei State Security Department and had targeted thousands of individuals and companies since at least 2010.
objective: Political and economic espionage, including transnational repression support

sources.label: DOJ press release on APT31 charges
State Department statement on actions against PRC cyber activity

name: APT40
summary: PRC MSS-linked actor highlighted by CISA and partner agencies for rapid exploitation of public proof-of-concept vulnerabilities and sustained regional espionage.
description: APT40 is a China-linked espionage actor that has repeatedly targeted governments and organizations in the Asia-Pacific region. A 2024 joint advisory from CISA, the FBI, NSA, ACSC, and partners described the group's tradecraft in action and noted its habit of rapidly weaponizing public exploit proof-of-concepts against vulnerable public-facing infrastructure.

sources.label: CISA advisory AA24-190A on APT40 tradecraft
CISA alert announcing APT40 advisory

name: APT41
summary: Chinese intrusion group described by the FBI as APT41/BARIUM and linked to broad global campaigns including supply-chain intrusions and telecom targeting.
description: APT41 is unusual in public reporting because it has been associated with both state-linked espionage and financially motivated activity. FBI material identifies named defendants as members of APT41/BARIUM and describes intrusions into hundreds of companies across sectors such as telecommunications, government, defense, social media, education, and manufacturing, including supply-chain attacks and ransomware deployment.

sources.label: FBI wanted page for APT41 group
DOJ charges against APT41 actors and associates
